scope: Repeated identical SPS and changed HEVC configuration at the same visible dimensions and frame rate, using official GStreamer 1.26.2 parser/core and the frozen private Cedar WC-v4/WC-v5 gst-omx sources.
summary: Repeated identical SPS does not automatically emit new parser caps or trigger gst-omx buffer reallocation.

A different GstCaps object or a different codec_data GstBuffer object with identical bytes is not by itself sufficient: parser and VideoDecoder compare caps values, and GstBuffer values compare size and contents.

The current broker forces byte-stream/AU at appsrc and at the parser output gate. The reviewed parser creates downstream codec_data only for hvc1/hev1 with AU alignment; the normal broker path therefore has NULL codec_data.

An accepted change to profile, level, tier, alignment, dimensions, or frame rate can trigger input-format reconfiguration even when visible dimensions stay 1920x1080. A metadata-only caps change need not do so.

OMX output-port settings events form a separate reallocation path. The wrapper increments a settings cookie without first checking dimensions, and an output settings event can cause buffer release/reallocation even when input caps and visible dimensions are unchanged.

Source review cannot establish whether the vendor decoder emits such an event for the current Bilibili SPS or whether its internal FBM changes. That requires runtime event/cookie/port-definition evidence. No board operation was performed for this review.

broker_backend.note: Working source snapshot identity, not proof of the currently installed broker binary.

parser_caps_path.finding: Each successfully parsed VPS and SPS sets update_caps=TRUE; PPS conditionally requests a check. This requests a caps check, not unconditional caps emission. Identical repeated SPS still passes through this check.
codec_data is built only for hvc1/hev1 output with AU alignment. New versus stored codec_data is compared by byte length and gst_buffer_memcmp, not pointer identity.

appsrc uses byte-stream/AU; parser disables passthrough and repeats configuration at IDR (config-interval=-1); output gate uses byte-stream/AU plus requested visible dimensions, 4:2:0 and 8-bit. appsrc deliberately omits dimensions so SPS can determine them.

Caps describe visible/cropped width and height, frame rate, chroma/bit depth, colorimetry, PAR, profile/tier/level and additional stream metadata. Equal visible dimensions and fps are not equivalent to equal full caps. Upstream supplied dimensions/framerate may override SPS in generic parser use; this broker omits them at appsrc.

After at least one output frame, existing codec_data is copied into candidate caps for equality testing so a midstream codec_data-only change does not resend caps. When new codec_data differs and the current frame lacks SPS or PPS, codec_data_modified is recorded. For byte-stream without codec_data, leftover codec_data is removed.

gst_pad_set_caps is called only when existing src caps and candidate caps are not gst_caps_is_strictly_equal. A codec_data-only change can instead set push_codec to inject updated parameter sets in-band at the next IDR.

videodecoder_caps_path.finding: gst_video_decoder_setcaps uses gst_caps_is_equal against its retained input state. Equal caps return TRUE without calling the subclass set_format, even if the GstCaps object address changes.
Only a caps value change creates a new input state and invokes subclass set_format. _new_input_state stores a caps reference and duplicates the boxed codec_data reference into state->codec_data.

GstBuffer value comparison fast-paths identical pointers but otherwise compares size and mapped bytes with memcmp. Identical codec_data bytes in a different GstBuffer object therefore compare equal, assuming successful mapping.

input_format_reconfiguration.finding: gst_omx_video_dec_set_format combines input port width, field height, Q16 frame rate, codec_data pointer inequality, and the codec subclass predicate. These checks run only after VideoDecoder accepts changed caps.

The H265 subclass is_format_change compares profile, level, tier and alignment strings. Thus a profile/level/tier/alignment change can trigger disable at identical visible dimensions and fps. This predicate does not compare all SPS bytes.

For a component already beyond Loaded, no real format change only updates input_state and returns. A real format change calls gst_omx_video_dec_disable. The state query uses an unbounded wait in both versions.

Disable drains, flushes output, disables ports and frees input/output buffers. The NO_COMPONENT_RECONFIGURE hack instead stops/closes/reopens the component. This is a real resource transition, not merely a caps reference update.
The next eligible input frame can enable the disabled component and allocate input buffers again. Output buffers are allocated by the applicable output-enable/reconfiguration path.

self->codec_data is pending CODECCONFIG input and is cleared to NULL after submission. Consequently a later nonidentical caps event with non-NULL codec_data can make the pointer predicate true even if the bytes match the original configuration. This is conditional on reaching set_format; it does not bypass the earlier caps equality checks and is ordinarily absent in this byte-stream pipeline.

independent_output_reconfiguration.finding: The OMX callback converts OMX_EventPortSettingsChanged into a queued settings-change message, applying configured event index quirks.

Message processing increments each matching port settings_cookie and refreshes its definition; output ports enter pending_reconfigure_outports. No width/height equality filter precedes the cookie increment.

Input acquisition waits for pending output reconfiguration. Output acquisition drains old pending buffers and then returns GST_OMX_ACQUIRE_BUFFER_RECONFIGURE when settings_cookie differs from configured_settings_cookie.

The output loop handles RECONFIGURE independently of input set_format. If the output port is enabled it disables it, waits for buffer release and deallocates output buffers, then runs reconfigure_output_port.
Output reconfiguration negotiates caps, allocates output buffers, populates the port and marks it reconfigured. Equal visible dimensions alone do not suppress this path.

case_matrix.case: Repeated identical SPS/VPS/PPS, stable emitted caps
case_matrix.input_caps_reallocation: No automatic caps event or set_format call; checks suppress equal caps.
case_matrix.output_reallocation: Not established; independent vendor settings events remain possible.

case_matrix.case: Different caps/codec_data object addresses, otherwise identical values
case_matrix.input_caps_reallocation: No automatic set_format call; semantic equality is the gate.

case_matrix.case: Changed SPS contents with identical visible dimensions, fps, profile, level, tier, alignment and all emitted caps fields
case_matrix.input_caps_reallocation: No input caps-triggered reallocation in the reviewed byte-stream path.
case_matrix.output_reallocation: Possible if vendor sends settings change, or vendor internal resources change; neither follows automatically from this source review.

case_matrix.case: Changed profile/level/tier or alignment at 1920x1080 with the same fps
case_matrix.input_caps_reallocation: Yes if changed caps are accepted and component is not Loaded, via H265 subclass predicate.

case_matrix.case: Only unrelated metadata changes, stable width/field-height/fps/profile/level/tier/alignment, NULL codec_data
case_matrix.input_caps_reallocation: set_format can run but returns after replacing input_state without disabling ports.
case_matrix.output_reallocation: Still determined by vendor settings events, not the metadata-only input path.

case_matrix.case: OMX output settings event, even with unchanged visible dimensions
case_matrix.output_reallocation: Yes when the event reaches the normal active output acquisition/reconfiguration path; errors or flushing may interrupt completion.

actionable_conclusions: Do not remove repeated SPS or weaken the current caps gate solely on the theory that every SPS/codec_data object forces OMX reallocation; that premise is false for the reviewed path.

For the retained decoder, compare full emitted caps and record OMX settings_cookie/configured_settings_cookie, event port/index, output port definition and allocation count across the stream boundary.
Distinguish parser caps change, VideoDecoder set_format, input-port disable, output-port settings change, and vendor-internal FBM allocation as separate events in evidence.
The existing visible-size/8-bit/4:2:0 gate does not prove stable coded layout, DPB requirements, SPS semantics, or absence of OMX output reconfiguration.

Any proposed broader retained-context reuse needs evidence that its accepted SPS changes do not consume additional quarantined DMA resources; current source review alone does not supply that evidence.
limits: Official parser/core source version is exact 1.26.2, but this review does not establish byte-for-byte source provenance for the installed private parser in /opt/t736-gst-parser-v27.
WC-v4/WC-v5 source identities were checked locally and/or by read-only SSH to the build host. No board SSH, serial, FEL, reboot, service control, deployment or recovery was used.
No dynamic repeated-SPS test was run. Findings describe the inspected control flow, not a verified cause of the current zero-output/idle failure.
This record contains source hashes, paths and conclusions only; no vendor binary or private media payload is included.
